--- title: "[markdown_to_commonmark()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Parse CommonMark/GFM and render back as normalized CommonMark. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/multimark/blob/main/src/multimark/_cmark.py#L598-L723){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python markdown_to_commonmark( text, *, hardbreaks=False, smart=False, normalize=False, unsafe=False, footnotes=False, extensions=(), width=0, options=0 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Parses the input Markdown into an AST and re-renders it as CommonMark. This effectively normalizes the formatting: different but semantically equivalent Markdown inputs (e.g., `*italic*` vs `_italic_`, varying list indentation) will produce a canonical output form. This is useful for round-trip testing, canonical formatting, or cleaning up inconsistently formatted documents. The output of this function, when parsed again, produces the same AST as the original input. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [text]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Markdown string to parse and normalize. Must be a Python `str`. [hardbreaks]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Render soft line breaks as hard breaks (backslash-newline). By default, this is `False`. [smart]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convert straight quotes to curly quotes, `--` to en-dashes, `---` to em-dashes, and `...` to ellipses. By default, this is `False`. [normalize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Consolidate adjacent text nodes in the parsed AST. By default, this is `False`. [unsafe]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Allow raw HTML to pass through. By default, this is `False`, which replaces raw HTML with a comment placeholder. [footnotes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Enable footnote syntax parsing. By default, this is `False`. [extensions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [()
]{.doc-parameter-default} : A sequence of GFM extension names to enable. Valid names are `"table"`, `"strikethrough"`, `"autolink"`, `"tagfilter"`, and `"tasklist"`. [width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column at which to wrap output lines. Set to `0` (the default) to disable line wrapping entirely. This is useful for producing line-wrapped output for version-control-friendly diffs. [options]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : An integer bitmask of `Options` flags (e.g., `Options.SMART | Options.UNSAFE`). Merged via OR with any boolean keyword arguments set to `True`. Defaults to `0`. ::: ## Keyword Arguments Vs. Options Flags {.doc-keyword-arguments-vs-options-flags} The boolean keyword arguments (`smart`, `unsafe`, `hardbreaks`, etc.) are convenience shortcuts for the most common `Options` flags. When both styles are provided, they are merged via OR. See `markdown_to_html()` for a detailed explanation. ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The normalized CommonMark string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Normalize inconsistent formatting: ::: {#04342f84 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import markdown_to_commonmark markdown_to_commonmark("_hello_ **world**") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '*hello* **world**\n' ``` ::: ::: Verify round-trip stability (parse, render, re-parse produces the same HTML): ::: {#1c104cd0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import markdown_to_commonmark, markdown_to_html original = "**bold** and *italic*" normalized = markdown_to_commonmark(original) assert markdown_to_html(original) == markdown_to_html(normalized) ``` ::: Wrap at 80 columns for version-control-friendly output: ::: {#623b5383 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} long_document = "This is a long sentence for demonstration. " * 10 print(markdown_to_commonmark(long_document, width=80)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. This is a long sentence for demonstration. ``` ::: :::
